question: What is the primary goal of performing last offices?

options.A: To treat the body with dignity and respect
options.B: To sanitize the hospital ward completely
options.C: To train junior student nurses on anatomy
options.D: To prepare the body immediately for autopsy

explanation: Last offices are carried out primarily to ensure the deceased person is handled with respect, care, and dignity. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h1)

question: Why is performing last offices calmly so important for the family?

options.A: It gives grieving relatives a sense of peace and comfort
options.B: It prevents the family from asking too many questions
options.C: It speeds up the process of issuing a death certificate
options.D: It proves to the doctor that death actually occurred

explanation: Seeing a loved one cared for gently and professionally helps reassure the family that the patient was valued until the very end. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h1)

question: What must legally happen before a nurse can begin last offices?

options.A: Arrival of the mortuary attendants at the ward
options.B: Formal certification of death by a physician
options.C: Payment of all hospital bills by the family
options.D: Completion of the police report for the incident

explanation: A doctor must officially confirm and document death before any last offices or body transfers can take place. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h2)

question: How should a nurse handle conflicting cultural or religious burial requests?

options.A: Accommodate the beliefs respectfully while following hospital policy
options.B: Refuse to participate in the care of the deceased patient
options.C: Ignore the family requests and follow standard hospital routine
options.D: Insist that the hospital rules override all personal beliefs

explanation: Nurses must balance standard safety protocols with deep respect for the cultural and religious traditions of the deceased and their family. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h2)

question: Why must a nurse wear PPE when performing last offices?

options.A: To protect against exposure to infectious body fluids
options.B: To comply with fire safety rules in the hospital
options.C: To prevent the family from recognizing the nurse later
options.D: To keep the nurse's uniform from getting wrinkled

explanation: Pathogens can still be present in bodily fluids after death, making standard precautions and PPE essential for staff safety. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of gathering all supplies before starting the procedure?

options.A: To complete the care efficiently without unnecessary delays
options.B: To ensure the doctor signs the paperwork on time
options.C: To make the hospital ward look neat to visitors
options.D: To prevent the family from entering the room early

explanation: Having everything ready at the bedside prevents the nurse from leaving the body unattended to fetch missing items. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h3)

question: In what position should the nurse place the body before rigor mortis sets in?

options.B: In a semi-Fowler position at 45 degrees
options.C: Prone with the head turned sideways

explanation: Placing the body flat in a supine position with straight limbs prevents stiffness in awkward postures. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h4)

question: A patient died with an IV line in place and a coroner's post-mortem is requested. What should the nurse do with the line?

options.A: Hide the lines under the bedsheets
options.B: Remove all lines immediately to clean the skin
options.C: Leave all lines and tubes in place
options.D: Cut the tubing short and tape it down

explanation: For coroner's cases or potential legal investigations, invasive lines and tubes must be left intact for the pathologist. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h4)

question: What is the safest way to handle a deceased patient's jewelry and cash?

options.A: Document them and hand them to family or hospital administration
options.B: Send them along with the body directly to the mortuary
options.C: Give them to the ward cleaner for safekeeping
options.D: Leave them securely locked inside the bedside drawer

explanation: Valuables must be formally documented and given to the family or administrative authorities to prevent loss or theft. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h5)

question: Why is it dangerous to leave jewelry on a patient when sending the body to the mortuary?

options.A: It makes the body bag too heavy to lift safely
options.B: It violates the medical license of the attending physician
options.C: It interferes with the natural cooling process of the body
options.D: It increases the risk of loss and creates unnecessary conflict

explanation: Unsecured valuables often go missing during body transfers, leading to serious accusations and distress for the family. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h5)

question: Which detail must be included in the nursing documentation after a patient dies?

options.A: The financial status of the patient's family
options.B: The exact time death was pronounced
options.C: The names of all nurses working on the next shift
options.D: The exact cause of the underlying disease

explanation: The exact time of death pronouncement by the doctor is a legal requirement that must be documented in the nursing notes. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h6)

question: Why should nurses participate in emotional debriefing after handling multiple patient deaths?

options.A: To fulfill mandatory hospital financial auditing rules
options.B: To prevent emotional burnout and maintain mental well-being
options.C: To practice their clinical writing and documentation skills
options.D: To learn how to avoid making errors on death certificates

explanation: Regularly dealing with loss takes an emotional toll, making peer support and debriefing essential for nursing self-care. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h6)
